germline mutations in TP53 cause a wide range of tumour types, including many that are rare in the general population.

Li-Fraumenie syndrome, a disorder with high penetrance of cancer, is a cancer predisposition syndrome with a spectrum of cancer types that includes brain tumours, soft tissue sarcoma, adrenocorticoid carcinoma, phyllodes tumours, osteosarcomas and breast carcinoma.

germline mutations in TP53 are associated with an increased risk of breast cancer, soft tissue sarcoma, osteosarcomas, brain tumours (particularly choroid plexus papilloma), adrenocorticoal carcinoma, Wilms tumour and phylodes tumour.

the spectrum of cancers associated with TP53 germline mutations is: breast cancer, soft tissue sarcoma, adrenocortex, osteosarcomas, brain tumours (astrocytomas), phyllodes tumours and Wilms' tumours.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
germline mutations of TP53 are associated with an increased risk of breast cancer, sarcomas, adrenocarcial carcinoma, phyllodes tumours and leukaemia.
germline mutations in TP53 increase the risk of a range of cancers including brain tumours, sarcomas and carcinomas of the breast, pancreas, adrenals and ovary.
germline mutations of p53 predispose to cancers of the breast, ovary and soft tissues, and to cancers of the adrenals, brain and pancreas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
germline p53 mutations do not increase general cancer risk but rather have tissue specific effects.
the spectrum and frequency of cancer types associated with germlin TP53 mutations is tissue specific.
germline mutations in the p53 gene cause a spectrum of cancers, but the most frequent cancers are not the most lethal.
